div.head: Introduction
div.p: The modern interpretation of siphonophore taxonomy has until recently been based on the comprehensive monograph of Totton (1965a), modified after several more recent authors. Additional work was reviewed by Mackie et al. (1987), and major contributions since 1987 include Margulis (1988), Pugh and Youngbluth (1988a and b), Pugh (1992aPugh ( -c, 1995Pugh ( , 1999aPugh ( and b, 2001Pugh ( ,2003Pugh ( ,2005Pugh ( , 2006a and b), Pugh andPages (1993, 1995), Carre and Carre (1995), Pages and Pugh (2002), Hissmann (2005), Mapstone (2003Mapstone ( , 2004Mapstone ( , 2005)), Dunn (2005), Dunn et al. (2005a and b), Haddock et al. (2005a and b), and Dunn and Wagner (2006). From this list, four recent papers, Haddock et al. (2005a), Dunn et al. (2005b), Dunn and Wagner (2006), and Pugh (2006b), provide the groundwork for a modern view of siphonophores.
